title: Cloud Drag and Drop
description:
- Dragging -\
When you are dragging the object, a cloud variable is set to 1. This is to prevent another device or person from dragging at the same time. Once you release, it is set to 0. If a user accidentally leaves the page, another user must wait 30 seconds by having the project check if the reported value of the days since 2000 block multiplied by 86400 minus the reported value of the cloud variable of the last time it was dragged multiplied by 86400 is greater than 30. to make sure they didn't disconnect and actually left the page. We only update cloud variables once every 0.1 seconds (and only one of the four variables), which complies with the limits of actual cloud variables. If you test on two devices, you can see it jumping horizontally and vertically while dragging on the other device because of Scratch's limitations. You will, however, be only able to drag on one device at one time.\

title: UNIX Time
description:
Algorithm:\
The number of seconds in a day is 86400. The number of days between January 1, 1970 and January 1, 2000 is 10,957, and 10,957 times 86400 is added to the number of days since the beginning of the year 2000 UTC multiplied by 86400. Then the whole result is rounded down.
instructions: UNIX time or Unix time: The number of seconds (rounded down) since January 1, 1970 at 12:00:00.000 AM UTC (Coordinated Universal Time)

title: Cloud List Engine
description:
- Notes -\
This project has no case sensing, as it is all lowercase for username encoding.\
You may wonder why you see an empty argument for a function in the code. This actually has an important purpose. This is only used if the Users-1 variable is empty; meaning the list just got archived, or you are the first one to upload your username to the cloud variable. The way the decryption function works is that it checks if a trailing zero at the beginning of the cloud variable was removed by checking if the string is even; if so, it adds a 0 in front and adds a repeat block. Although it could (but shouldn't) report the value of the cloud variable, cloud variables are created as 0 by default; they cannot be blank. The function will tell the computer to decrypt 00; 00 signifies the end of a username, so an empty username would be added at the end of the list, as it will just be read as 00. If it was read as something like \11030809010503273500\"
datetime_created: it would decode as a list containing one item named \"kchiaec19\".\

(Important: All instructions below are for @-ReadyBoy- only.)\
- How to Backup Ratings -\
Press the B key to save backups.\
Answer the prompt to confirm.\
Wait for the backup code to generate.\
Triple-click the list item to select it.\
Press Ctrl+C or right-click on the selected part → Copy.\
Save it somewhere by creating a new text box or overwriting the previous text box (for overwriting existing backups) that can save in a program or website that can save text and pressing Ctrl+V or right-click on the text box → Paste.\
Click outside of the list to hide the save code. Make sure you saved it somewhere beforehand!\
- How to Restore Backups -\
Press the R key to restore backups.\

love_count:
There is a New Scratcher detector.\
Use the mouse by clicking on the buttons. Button legend:\
Numbers - Type in a number and it may add to the number you entered. If you type a number when the number you've entered is exactly 256 characters (to match cloud limits when setting combinations), you will be alerted.\
C - Stands for Clear. Undoes the last digit you entered if there is one. If not, you'll be alerted.\
E - Stands for Enter. Either checks if the current combination is right, or sets it as a new combination if there are none and you didn't try to set an empty combination (you will also be prompted to type in what items you want for the safe). Also clears out the number you entered.\
You won't be able to see what items are in the safe unless it is unlocked.\
To prevent conflicting uploads, there's a queue. It can also check if someone left during the upload. This is to prevent two people from setting a combination at once. It also checks if the safe is still unlocked once the queue clears out.\
If you find any inappropriate items in the safe when you unlock it (or when it is already unlocked), please post a comment saying what username you see in the variable called \user who last locked the safe\" (who also inputted the items) and what you saw for the variable \"items in the safe\". I will then check the cloud data logs to confirm. If you are right
favorite_count: I will give the other user (the one acting inappropriately) a strike. If you are wrong (with the exception of typos; in this case
instructions: I will give the other user a strike)
language: the commenter (the accusing player) will get a strike. After a specific user gets three strikes (I may also include alternate accounts if they mention about it)
column12: they won't be allowed to use the project anymore. I may take back a strike from a username for reasons such as a typo in the username I entered
column13: or if the user became respectful or was hacked at the time. The strike system is used only to teach users a lesson not to put inappropriate content in places where everyone can see it (e.g. cloud variables). Nothing will happen to the user on the first or second strike for now. I plan on adding these features later.\

title: Monospace Text Engine (First Remix)
description:
*Still trying to implement word wrapping, this might take a while.*\
Please don't worry on the slides where you have to move your mouse if you're on a touchscreen, because you won't get to the next slide until you release the mouse.\
You will find a slide that will prompt you for an answer right away. However, unless you tell it to, the asking prompt never stops after any amount of time. Therefore, it will always wait for your turn. You can enter an answer after you have read and understood all the text in the slide.\
There is also an external Scratch player detector from the Scratch Wiki, which is used to determine how it returns an error when not played on Scratch.\
This engine supports all 95 standard characters supported on an American English QWERTY keyboard and is case-sensitive.\
Credit to @djpro for inspiration and the idea of using question marks to replace unsupported characters (I modified the idea after).\
Credit to @-Rex- for the idea of putting the tutorial in the Stage.\
Credit to @joshiesays for the recursive thumbnail tutorial!\
(Sorry, sometimes words get broken off before they finish.)\
One credit I can't seem to find the original owner of - does anyone know? (Please see the Stage if you don't know what I'm talking about.)\
Please note: I decided to convert the letters to bitmap because the font rendered differently on my other device. Also, although the monospace font is exactly the same in both the thumbnail and the text engine sprite, it just shows the rendering of the same font in two different OSs.\
\
For this to truly be monospace, I set some variables containing the width and height each character and line must be apart. These values are the height of the highest character in the entire list of character costumes and the width of the widest character in the entire list of character costumes. I determined these by creating two lists: one for heights and one for widths. Then, I exported both lists; finally, I used a website to sort the file contents numerically - so I can easily determine the highest value in the sorted lists. I also made sure to carefully check the lists both before and after every step.\
\
Credit to @qucchia for the original project!\

description:
A visible factor number is a number that is divisible by each of its non-zero digits. It is a little-known thing, and when someone tried to create a Wikipedia page about it, it got deleted. The first portion of this sequence is also present in https://oeis.org/A002796.\
\
